stories.title: POS Loyalty Summary Display on Customer Identification
stories.user_story: As Sana (store associate), I want to see a customer's loyalty summary when I identify them at POS, so that I can personalize their checkout experience
acceptance_criteria: Given a customer is identified via phone, loyalty ID, or QR scan, When the lookup completes, Then the POS displays: customer name, tier badge with color, current points balance, monetary equivalent, member since date, and lifetime points earned within 2 seconds
Given the loyalty summary is displayed, When I view the last transactions section, Then the 3 most recent transactions are shown with date, type, and points amount
Given a customer is identified, When the API response includes tier benefits, Then a personalization hint is displayed (e.g., 'Gold member — eligible for 10% bonus')
Given the POS loyalty panel, When accessed via keyboard navigation, Then all elements are reachable and the panel is announced by screen readers with appropriate labels

requirements_used: FR-03 — POS Loyalty Status Display — tier, balance, membership status within 2 seconds

stories.reasoning: 5 points: API integration + UI panel + personalization hints. 2-second SLA from NFR-01. Confidential because it displays customer PII and financial data. Accessibility AC included for user-facing POS screen.

stories.title: POS Display — Customer Not Found Handling
stories.user_story: As Sana (store associate), I want clear guidance when a customer is not found in the loyalty system, so that I can offer them registration instead of a dead end
acceptance_criteria: Given a lookup is performed with a phone/loyalty ID/QR that matches no customer, When the API returns 404, Then the POS displays 'Not a loyalty member' with a prominent 'Register Customer' action button
Given the 'Register Customer' button is tapped, When the registration flow starts, Then it pre-fills the lookup value (e.g., phone number) into the in-store registration form
Given the lookup API is unavailable or times out after 5 seconds, When the error occurs, Then the POS shows 'Loyalty service temporarily unavailable — proceed without loyalty' and logs the failure
stories.reasoning: 3 points: negative path story covering not-found and timeout scenarios. Pre-filling lookup value reduces friction for in-store registration. Timeout handling ensures POS checkout isn't blocked by loyalty system failures.

stories.title: Manual Points Addition by Store Staff
stories.user_story: As Sana (store associate), I want to manually add points to a customer's account with a reason, so that I can resolve issues like missed accruals or provide goodwill gestures
acceptance_criteria: Given I select a customer and choose 'Add Points', When I enter points amount (≤ 500), select a reason from the predefined list (system_error_correction, goodwill_gesture, promotional_credit, other), and submit, Then the points are immediately credited and a success confirmation is shown
Given I select reason 'other', When the form is displayed, Then a free-text notes field becomes required and must contain at least 10 characters
Given the adjustment is submitted, When it is processed, Then an audit record is created with: staff_id, customer_id, action='add', points, reason, notes, timestamp, and approval_status='approved'
Given the adjustment succeeds, When the customer is notified, Then they receive a push notification: '{points} points added — Reason: {reason}. New balance: {balance}.'

requirements_used: FR-10 — Manual Points Adjustment — add/deduct, reason selection, manager approval above threshold, audit logged

stories.reasoning: 5 points: form + validation + ledger write + audit + notification. Separated add from deduct for clarity. ≤500 threshold allows immediate processing without manager approval.

stories.title: Manual Points Deduction by Store Staff
stories.user_story: As Sana (store associate), I want to manually deduct points from a customer's account with a documented reason, so that I can correct errors or handle fraud cases
acceptance_criteria: Given I select a customer and choose 'Deduct Points', When I enter points amount (≤ 500), select a reason (system_error_correction, fraud_correction, other), and submit, Then the points are immediately deducted and a confirmation is shown
Given the deduction would result in a negative balance, When I submit, Then the system shows an error: 'Customer only has {balance} points available. Maximum deduction: {balance} points.'
Given the deduction succeeds, When the customer is notified, Then they receive: '{points} points deducted — Reason: {reason}. New balance: {balance}.'

requirements_used: FR-10 — Manual Points Adjustment — add/deduct, reason selection, audit logged

stories.reasoning: 3 points: reuses adjustment infrastructure from US-062 but adds negative balance validation. Negative path AC prevents over-deduction.

stories.title: Manager Approval for Large Adjustments
stories.user_story: As Sana (store associate), I want large point adjustments (> 500) to require manager approval, so that high-value changes have dual-control oversight
acceptance_criteria: Given I submit an adjustment exceeding 500 points, When the request is created, Then it enters 'pending_approval' state and I see: 'Adjustment requires manager approval. Reference: {ref_id}'
Given a pending adjustment exists, When a user with 'loyalty_manager' role reviews it, Then they can approve or reject with an optional note
Given a manager approves the adjustment, When approval is recorded, Then the points are credited/deducted, the customer is notified, and the audit record includes approver_id
Given a manager rejects the adjustment, When rejection is recorded, Then the requesting staff is notified with the rejection reason and no points are moved
Given the adjustment API, When called by a user without 'loyalty_staff' or 'loyalty_manager' role, Then it returns 403 Forbidden

requirements_used: FR-10 — Manual Points Adjustment — manager approval above threshold

stories.reasoning: 5 points: approval workflow + role checks + notification to staff. Dual-control follows SOX segregation of duties. Security AC for role authorization included.

stories.title: Automatic Retry for Failed Points Accrual
stories.user_story: As Clara (loyalty customer), I want the system to automatically retry when my points accrual fails, so that transient errors don't cause me to lose points
acceptance_criteria: Given a points accrual fails due to system_error or timeout, When the failure is detected, Then the transaction is queued for automatic retry with exponential backoff (1min, 5min, 30min)
Given a retry succeeds on attempt 2 or 3, When points are credited, Then the standard accrual notification is sent and no failure notification is triggered
Given all 3 retry attempts fail, When the final retry exhausts, Then the transaction is marked as 'failed' and a failure notification is queued for the customer

requirements_used: FR-11 — Failed Accrual Notification — notify within 5 minutes, explain issue, provide resolution instructions

stories.reasoning: 3 points: retry queue + backoff logic + conditional notification. Resolves most transient failures silently. Only notifies customer after all retries exhausted.

stories.title: Failed Accrual Customer Notification
stories.user_story: As Clara (loyalty customer), I want to be notified when my points accrual permanently fails, so that I know to contact support with my receipt
acceptance_criteria: Given all retry attempts have failed, When the failure notification is sent, Then it is delivered within 5 minutes of the final retry: 'We couldn't add points for your purchase on {date} ({order_id}). Please contact support or visit any store with your receipt. Reference: {failure_id}'
Given a failed accrual exists, When I view my transaction history, Then it appears with a 'failed' badge and the failure reference ID
Given the notification is sent, When a support ticket reference is created, Then store staff can look up the failure_id to process a manual adjustment

requirements_used: FR-11 — Failed Accrual Notification — notify within 5 minutes, explain issue, provide resolution instructions

stories.reasoning: 3 points: notification template + history badge + support reference. 5-minute SLA gives time for retries before notifying. Links to manual adjustment (F-05.2) for resolution.

stories.title: Failed Accrual — Non-Retryable Errors
stories.user_story: As a platform engineer, I want non-retryable accrual failures (customer_not_found, duplicate_transaction) to be handled differently from transient errors, so that the system doesn't waste resources retrying impossible operations
acceptance_criteria: Given an accrual fails because the transaction_id already exists, When the duplicate is detected, Then it is rejected immediately with no retry and logged as 'duplicate_rejected'
Given an accrual fails because the customer_id is not found, When the failure is detected, Then it is placed in a dead-letter queue for manual review (customer may not be linked yet)
Given a dead-letter queue item exists, When an admin reviews it, Then they can retry (after linking customer) or discard with a reason
stories.reasoning: 3 points: error classification + DLQ + admin review UI. Negative path story ensuring non-retryable errors don't loop. Duplicate rejection prevents double-crediting.

stories.title: Immutable Audit Log for State Changes
stories.user_story: As a compliance officer, I want all state-changing operations logged immutably with full context, so that I can reconstruct any event for audit or investigation purposes
acceptance_criteria: Given any state-changing operation occurs (points_earned, points_redeemed, points_adjusted, profile_updated, account_created, config_changed, tier_changed), When it completes, Then an audit entry is created with: event_id (UUID), timestamp, actor_type, actor_id, action, entity_type, entity_id, before_state, after_state, source_system, ip_address, correlation_id
Given the audit log table, When any database user attempts UPDATE or DELETE, Then the operation is denied by database permissions (append-only enforcement)
Given audit records exist, When retention policy is evaluated, Then records are retained for 7 years minimum
Given the audit log contains PII references, When accessed, Then only users with 'loyalty_admin' or 'compliance' role can query it, and access itself is logged

requirements_used: FR-28 — System Audit Trail — all state changes logged with actor, timestamp, action, before/after, source system. Immutable, retained per policy.

stories.reasoning: 5 points: schema design + append-only enforcement + retention config + RBAC. Restricted sensitivity because audit logs contain complete operational history. Security AC for access control on Restricted data.

stories.title: Audit Log Query API & Export
stories.user_story: As a compliance officer, I want to query and export audit logs by customer, action, or date range, so that I can produce evidence for audits and investigations
acceptance_criteria: Given I am authenticated with 'loyalty_admin' or 'compliance' role, When I call GET /v1/admin/audit with filters (customer_id, action, from, to), Then matching audit entries are returned paginated (50 per page) sorted by timestamp descending
Given a query returns results, When I request CSV export, Then a downloadable file is generated with all matching records within 30 seconds for up to 10,000 records
Given I am authenticated without admin/compliance role, When I call the audit API, Then I receive 403 Forbidden

requirements_used: FR-28 — System Audit Trail — query and export capabilities

stories.reasoning: 3 points: query API + CSV export + authorization. Depends on audit log existing (US-068). Security AC for role-based access on Restricted data.

stories.title: Staff Authentication via Employee Credentials
stories.user_story: As Sana (store associate), I want to log in to the loyalty system using my employee credentials, so that my actions are tracked and I can access staff-only features
acceptance_criteria: Given I am a store associate, When I enter my employee ID and password on the staff login screen, Then I am authenticated and issued a short-lived token (4-hour expiry) with my role claims
Given my token has expired after 4 hours, When I attempt any staff action, Then I am redirected to re-authenticate (no refresh token — shift-based sessions)
Given I enter incorrect credentials 5 times consecutively, When the 5th attempt fails, Then my account is locked for 30 minutes and a security alert is logged
Given the staff login screen, When navigated via keyboard, Then all form fields and buttons are accessible with visible focus indicators

requirements_used: FR-10 — Manual Points Adjustment — requires authorized store associates
FR-28 — System Audit Trail — actor identification

stories.reasoning: 5 points: auth flow + short-lived tokens + lockout + role claims. Restricted because credentials are highest-sensitivity. 4-hour expiry prevents abandoned terminal exploitation. Security AC for lockout and access control.

stories.title: SSO Integration for Staff & Admin Users
stories.user_story: As a platform engineer, I want staff authentication to integrate with the client's identity provider via SSO, so that employee lifecycle management is centralized
acceptance_criteria: Given the client's identity provider (Active Directory/Okta) is configured, When a staff member clicks 'Sign in with SSO', Then they are redirected to the IdP, authenticate, and return with a valid staff token containing role claims mapped from directory groups
Given a staff member is deactivated in the directory, When their token expires or they attempt re-authentication, Then access is denied immediately
Given SSO is configured, When the IdP is unavailable, Then a fallback to employee ID + password is available with a warning banner: 'SSO unavailable — using local authentication'
stories.reasoning: 5 points: OIDC/SAML integration + group-to-role mapping + fallback. Restricted sensitivity for credential handling. SSO ensures employee offboarding immediately revokes loyalty system access.

stories.title: Role-Based Access Control for Staff Operations
stories.user_story: As a platform engineer, I want staff API endpoints protected by role-based access control, so that associates, managers, and admins can only perform actions appropriate to their role
acceptance_criteria: Given a user with 'loyalty_staff' role, When they call adjustment, customer lookup, or earn/redeem APIs, Then access is granted
Given a user with 'loyalty_staff' role, When they call approval, reporting, or configuration APIs, Then they receive 403 Forbidden
Given a user with 'loyalty_manager' role, When they call approval endpoints, Then access is granted in addition to all staff permissions
Given a user with 'loyalty_admin' role, When they call any staff or admin endpoint, Then access is granted (full system access)
Given any staff endpoint is called, When the request is processed, Then the actor's role and terminal_id (if POS) are included in the audit trail

requirements_used: FR-28 — actor identification for all operations

stories.reasoning: 3 points: middleware + role hierarchy + audit enrichment. Restricted because RBAC config is security-sensitive. Follows least-privilege principle with escalating permissions.

stories.title: MFA Requirement for Manager & Admin Roles
stories.user_story: As a security engineer, I want MFA enforced for manager and admin role logins, so that elevated privileges require stronger authentication
acceptance_criteria: Given a user with 'loyalty_manager' or 'loyalty_admin' role authenticates, When primary credentials are verified, Then they are prompted for a second factor (TOTP or push notification) before a token is issued
Given MFA is required, When the second factor is not provided within 5 minutes, Then the authentication session expires and the user must restart login
Given a user with 'loyalty_staff' role authenticates, When primary credentials are verified, Then no MFA is required and a token is issued immediately
stories.reasoning: 3 points: MFA integration + conditional enforcement by role. Restricted sensitivity. MFA for elevated roles follows enterprise security standards and prevents credential theft from granting admin access.

stories.title: POS Terminal Device Authentication
stories.user_story: As a platform engineer, I want POS terminals to authenticate at the device level, so that transactions can be traced to specific terminals for audit purposes
acceptance_criteria: Given a POS terminal is registered in the system, When a staff member authenticates on that terminal, Then the issued token includes a terminal_id claim alongside the staff identity
Given a transaction is processed from a POS terminal, When the audit record is created, Then it includes both staff_id and terminal_id for full traceability
Given a terminal_id is not recognized, When a request is made, Then it is rejected with 403 and a security alert is raised

requirements_used: FR-28 — System Audit Trail — source system identification

stories.reasoning: 3 points: device registration + token enrichment + unknown device rejection. Restricted because device auth config is security-sensitive. Enables per-terminal fraud detection.

regression_summary.recommendation: Greenfield — no regression testing needed. All stories are new capabilities.
